text: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
Hear the terms of this covenant, and speak them to the people of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
Say to them: This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Cursed is the one who does not obey the terms of this covenant,

which I commanded your fathers on the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the iron furnace, saying, "Listen to my voice and do everything I command you, and you will be my people and I will be your God"—
so that I might fulfill the oath I swore to your fathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is today. And I answered, "Amen, LORD."
Then the LORD said to me: Proclaim all these words in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem: Hear the terms of this covenant and carry them out.
For I solemnly warned your fathers on the day I brought them up from the land of Egypt, and I have warned them again and again to this very day, saying, "Listen to my voice."

But they did not listen or pay attention; each followed the stubbornness of his own evil heart. So I brought upon them all the words of this covenant, which I had commanded them to keep but they did not keep.
The LORD said to me: A conspiracy has been found among the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

They have gone back to the sins of their forefathers, who refused to listen to my words; they have followed other gods to serve them. The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken the covenant I made with their fathers.
Therefore this is what the LORD says: I am about to bring on them a disaster they cannot escape. Though they cry out to me, I will not listen to them.
Then the cities of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem will go and cry out to the gods to whom they burn incense, but those gods will not save them at all in the time of their trouble.
For your gods have become as many as your cities, Judah; and the altars you have set up to that shameful thing are as many as the streets of Jerusalem—altars for burning incense to Baal.

versions.text: For you have as many gods as you have cities, Judah; and as many altars as there are streets in Jerusalem you have set up to that shameful thing, altars for burning incense to Baal.
versions.explanation: The second half is hard to follow when read aloud because the object ("as many altars as there are streets") is separated from its verb. Recasting keeps the parallelism of the Hebrew ("the number of your cities" / "the number of Jerusalem's streets") and flows better orally.

text: As for you, do not pray for this people or raise up any plea or petition for them, for I will not listen when they call to me in the time of their trouble.
What is my beloved doing in my house, carrying out her vile schemes with the crowd? Can consecrated flesh avert your doom? When you do evil, then you rejoice.
The LORD once called you a thriving olive tree, lovely in form and fruit. But with the roar of a mighty storm he has set it on fire, and its branches are broken.

versions.text: The LORD once called you a thriving olive tree, beautiful with fruit. But with the roar of a mighty storm he has set it on fire, and its branches are broken.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew phrase joins "fruit" and "form/appearance" (תֹאַר); "beautiful with fruit" drops the second element. "Lovely in form and fruit" is both more accurate and more rhythmic.

text: The LORD of hosts, who planted you, has decreed disaster for you, because of the evil the house of Israel and the house of Judah have done, provoking me to anger by burning incense to Baal.
The LORD made it known to me, and I knew; you showed me what they were doing.

But I was like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter; I did not know that they were plotting against me, saying, "Let us destroy the tree with its fruit; let us cut him off from the land of the living, so that his name will be remembered no more."

versions.text: I had been like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter; I did not know that they were plotting against me, saying, "Let us destroy the tree with its fruit; let us cut him off from the land of the living, so that his name will be remembered no more."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has a simple contrastive "But I..."; the English pluperfect "I had been" is heavier than needed and slightly obscures the contrast. "But I was" reads more naturally aloud.

text: But you, LORD of hosts, who judge righteously and test the heart and mind, let me see your vengeance upon them, for to you I have committed my cause.
Therefore this is what the LORD says about the men of Anathoth who are seeking your life and saying, "Do not prophesy in the name of the LORD, or you will die by our hands"—
therefore this is what the LORD of hosts says: I am about to punish them. Their young men will die by the sword, their sons and daughters by famine.

versions.text: therefore this is what the LORD of hosts says: I will punish them. Their young men will die by the sword, their sons and daughters by famine.
versions.explanation: הִנְנִי with the participle expresses imminent action ("Look, I am about to..."), as rendered elsewhere in this chapter (v. 11). The present rendering flattens the announcement formula.

text: Not even a remnant will be left to them, for I will bring disaster on the men of Anathoth in the year of their reckoning.
